patterns.block_scope_state_reset: R63 #aw_sg63a1 bufferresetbeforereuse: a write/read/reset state machine re-initialized fresh PER *ast.BlockStmt (analyzeStraightLineBlock's written/read maps), combined with collectEvents refusing to descend into If/For/Range/Switch/TypeSwitch/Select, means state never carries from an outer block into a nested control-flow block. A write+read in the outer scope followed by a reuse-write inside a nested if/for is invisible - the inner block's isolated event list sees only a first-ever write. PROBE any linter/analyzer that (a) walks every BlockStmt via ast.Inspect calling a per-block analysis function, AND (b) has that per-block function refuse to descend into sibling control-flow bodies - the two together silently sever state that should span the whole function. PROBE any new linter that walks blocks independently for a per-block-only forward search.
patterns.idiom_reflag_no_allowlist: R67 #61024 blankassigncomma (71st linter, first audit): a bare-syntax rule (2+ consecutive blank identifiers on an assignment LHS) with no allow-list or comment-aware exception re-flags an already-established codebase idiom for explicitly discarding a guaranteed-safe or non-critical return value (14 prod sites found, one with an explicit gosec-satisfying comment one line above it: hash.Hash.Write never returns an error in practice, but check to satisfy gosec G104). Root cause class: the new linter targets exactly the syntactic shape that contributors already use as the MANUAL workaround for a different, broken or disabled tool (here, errcheck exclude-functions, disabled in .golangci.yml:37) - so the new rule fights the old rules own accepted workaround instead of the actual bug. PROBE any new linter whose target pattern (a) has zero type-awareness of a well-known safe-to-ignore return contract (hash.Hash.Write, Close() on some best-effort cleanup, etc), and (b) is not cross-checked against grep of the real codebase before deciding readiness - a rule with a very simple AST shape and no allow-list is the highest-risk case for this class.
patterns.paren_unwrap_gap: R69 #61519 nilctxpassed: isBuiltinNil does a bare expr.(*ast.Ident) type assertion with no call to astutil.UnwrapParenExpr first, so f((nil)) escapes. R70 #61715: SAME class found twice more - errstringmatch isErrDotError type-asserts outer.Args[0] straight to *ast.CallExpr (err.Error() call) with no unwrap (CI-enforced); sprintfbool type-asserts call.Args[0] straight to *ast.BasicLit (format-string literal) with no unwrap (not yet enforced). Reference fix idiom used correctly elsewhere: walkfuncerrshadow/mapdeletecheck/packagelevelmutableslicemap, and the new 72nd linter typeassertionokdiscarded (via astutil.TwoValueTypeAssertionOKIdent, which unwraps ParenExpr on its own). PROBE any linter that type-asserts directly on an *ast.Ident/*ast.BasicLit/*ast.CallExpr for a builtin literal, string literal, or specific call shape without first calling astutil.UnwrapParenExpr - vein still open, try tolowerequalfold/mapclearloop/appendoneelement next.
